rows.note: Use this specifically for medical care or treatment involving intensive monitoring and life support, as in 深切治療部.

example.english: They are still in the intensive care unit and need close monitoring.
example.traditional: 佢而家仲留喺深切治療部，要密切觀察。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 lau4 hai2 sam1 cit3 zi6 liu4 bou6 jiu3 mat6 cit3 gun1 caat3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a course, schedule, or period packed with activity in a short time.

example.english: We signed up for an intensive Cantonese course and will finish it in two weeks.
example.traditional: 我哋報咗個密集式廣東話班，兩個星期就上完。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 bou3 zo2 go3 mat6 zaap6 sik1 gwong2 dung1 waa2 baan1 loeng5 go3 sing1 kei4 zau6 soeng5 jyun4

rows.note: Use this before a noun when the activity or process requires unusually large amounts of labour, money, materials, or other resources.

example.english: This industry is intensive in its use of resources, so it is not easy to develop in Hong Kong.
example.traditional: 呢種資源密集型工業，需要好多勞工同資金，唔係咁易喺香港發展。
